title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets' study the loop/braid relations of the Teichmüller tower (Γ_{0,3}, Γ_{1,1}, ... ; Γ_{1,1}=SL2(Z) is generated by an order-4 element σ and an order-6 element ρ). Here Grothendieck linearises the problem over a base S. He works in G=GL2 over S with an element σ (σ^2=u) and an element ρ (ρ^2-ρ-u=0, by (12) of the previous page). He uses the commutative 'tori' T_σ and T_ρ: the unit-group schemes of O_S[σ] and O_S[ρ], i.e. the centralisers of σ and ρ. N'_σ is the subgroup of elements normalising σ up to sign, sitting in an extension 1→T_σ→N'_σ→μ2→1. B'_0 = T_0·L_0 is the 'mirabolic' Borel, with T_0 = diag(μ,1) and L_0 the upper unipotent group. The previous page sets G*_{ρ,σ} = B'_0×T_ρ×N'_σ.

On this page:
(16) M_{ρ,σ}[0] ⊂ G*_{ρ,σ} is the subgroup of triples (u,a,b) with det u = det b = ε'·det a, ε'^2=1. These are triples whose determinants agree up to a sign on the T_ρ factor.
(17) M_{ρ,σ}(0) = M[0] ∩ (T_0×T_ρ×N'_σ). The written condition 'u=1' should be read as 'unipotent part of u trivial'.
(18) L_0 embeds as λ ↦ (ε_0(λ),1,1). This lands in M[0] since det ε_0(λ)=1.
(19) Hence M[0] = M(0)⋉L_0, a semidirect product with L_0 normal, induced from B'_0 = T_0⋉L_0.
(20) There is a character (χ, ε_2, ε_3): M[0] → G_m×μ2×μ2, where χ = det u = det b, ε_2 = ε_σ(b) is the sign from (14), and ε_3 = det a/det b ∈ μ2. It kills L_0, so it factors through the quotient.
(21) T_{ρ,σ} := M[0]/L_0.
(22)-(23) Since M(0)∩L_0 = 1 and M[0] = M(0)L_0, the composite M(0) → M[0] → T_{ρ,σ} is an isomorphism. So T_{ρ,σ} ≅ M(0) ⊂ T_0×T_ρ×N'_σ.
Next page: projecting to T_ρ×N'_σ is still a monomorphism, because det: T_0 ≅ G_m. The kernel of (ε_2, ε_3) is T° ≅ T_ρ ×_{G_m} T_σ, with 1→ST_ρ×ST_σ→T°→G_m→1. T_{ρ,σ} acts on SL2 through T_0 ⊂ PGL2, scaling L_0 by χ.

Purpose: build a 'diagonalisable-type' group scheme T_{ρ,σ} of symmetries of the configuration (B'_0, ρ, σ). It carries a G_m-character χ (a cyclotomic-type character) and two sign characters. It plays, at the level of SL2 / linear models of Γ_{1,1} and Γ_{0,3}, the role of the 'torus' of automorphisms in the Teichmüller-tower formalism. The ink margin note says Grothendieck himself found the notation T_{ρ,σ} unfortunate because of the clash with Γ_{ρ,σ}, Γ_{g,ν}, Γ_{0,3}.
errors: (17) 'défini par u=1' is sloppy: the intended condition is that u lies in T_0 (trivial unipotent component), as the second line M(0)=M[0]∩(T_0×T_ρ×N'_σ) makes clear.
ε_3 is written as det a/det b here; with the convention det b = ε' det a it equals ε'^{-1}=ε', which is consistent since ε'∈μ2. The next page's 'det a/det b = det b/det a' is likewise fine.
(18) should read λ ↦ (ε_0(λ),1,1); writing λ for ε_0(λ) is harmless abuse of notation.

ideas.what: Subgroup of B'_0×T_ρ×N'_σ cut out by determinant matching up to sign, written as a semidirect product with the unipotent L_0, whose quotient is a torus-by-(μ2×μ2) group T_{ρ,σ} with characters (χ, ε_2, ε_3)
ideas.modern_name: Levi decomposition / semidirect product of a solvable group scheme; extension of a finite diagonalisable group by a torus (fibre product of norm tori T_ρ ×_{G_m} T_σ)
ideas.where_published: Technique is SGA3-standard; this specific construction appears only in these unpublished notes as far as I know

ideas.what: Linearised (GL2/SL2 over a base S) model of the generators σ, ρ of Γ_{1,1}=SL2(Z) and their centraliser tori, serving the 'équation des lacets' programme
ideas.modern_name: group-scheme / linear-representation shadow of Grothendieck–Teichmüller symmetries; norm tori of quadratic algebras O_S[σ], O_S[ρ]
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse/Longue Marche program); GT developed by Drinfeld, Ihara
ideas.where_published: Possibly related to La Longue Marche (1981); not in Esquisse in this form

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up a G_m×μ2×μ2-graded group scheme T_{ρ,σ} of symmetries of the (ρ,σ) configuration in GL2 over an arbitrary base. Its character χ acts on L_0 by scaling, an algebraic analogue of the cyclotomic character on Γ_{1,1}-type data. This is a linear-algebraic (SL2-level) version of the torus/character structure later central in GT and graded GRT theory. It is a thread toward an algebraic-group model of the Teichmüller tower symmetries that does not seem to have been pursued in the literature in this form.
missed.quote: On a un homomorphisme M_{ρ,σ}[0] → G_m×μ2×μ2 noté g ↦ χ(g),ε_2(g),ε_3(g) ... trivial sur L_0
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Could suggest an elementary algebraic-group model of the GT/GRT G_m-action at the level of the SL2 quotient of Γ_{1,1}. The connection is speculative and the page itself is routine group-scheme bookkeeping.

deep.surprise_reason: The computations are correct but routine (semidirect product decomposition, quotient torus with sign characters). Interest lies only in the context: an unpublished linear-algebraic setup within the loop-equation programme, without a new result on this page.
transcription_corrections: Top-left margin list likely reads M_{ρ,σ}[0], M_{ρ,σ}(0), T_{ρ,σ}, T°_{ρ,σ}, B_{ρ,σ}, G*_{ρ,σ}, M_{ρ,σ}, T°*_{ρ,σ}. The 'B_{ρ,σ}' looks like a script G/B overwritten, matching the G*_{ρ,σ} of (16), whose letter in the image is also overwritten (B→G).
(18): λ ↦ (λ,1,1) as in the image, meaning (ε_0(λ),1,1).
(21) 'On pose ainsi' is better read 'On passe au quotient': T_{ρ,σ} ≃ M_{ρ,σ}[0]/L_0, et le composé ... (22) est un iso, d'où (23).
(23) the image shows M_{ρ,σ}(0) ≃ T_{ρ,σ} ↪ T_0×T_ρ×N'_σ, with the M overwritten.

Ink margin roughly: 'Cette notation n'est pas des plus heureuses (en principe, tout au moins, à cause de T_{ρ,σ}) ... la notation imposée par contrainte [?] ... Γ_{ρ,σ}, Γ_{g,ν} et Γ_{0,3}'. It is largely illegible; the gist is a notational clash with Γ_{ρ,σ}, Γ_{g,ν}, Γ_{0,3}.
